A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PIR forecasting framework. Their text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A-F are readable and can be matched reliably despite added material and pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting experiments, component ablations, sensitivity analysis and forecasting case studies in Section 4 and Appendices B-E.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds inference-time comparisons and model-depth/pretraining ablations in Tables 2 and 7.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains PIR's error estimator, local attention-based revision, cosine top-K global retrieval, weighted fusion and losses in Equations (1)-(7). LSH retrieval and scratch training appear as experimental comparison variants, without replacing the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same ETT, Electricity, Solar, Weather, Traffic, PEMS, Energy and Health datasets and retain long-term, short-term and text-assisted forecasting coverage. The new timing and ablation studies reuse existing datasets.

E2.justification: The four principal backbones remain PatchTST, SparseTSF, iTransformer and TimeMixer. v2 additionally compares cosine retrieval with LSH in Table 2 and introduces deepened iTransformer and PIR trained from scratch as controls in Table 7.

E3.justification: v2 adds average inference-time measurements with backbone/retrieval/revision breakdowns and controls that match additional layer depth or remove backbone pretraining. The original splits, forecast horizons, MSE/MAE metrics and stated optimization settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 supplements the retained auxiliary-loss sensitivity, component ablations and case studies with computational-overhead analysis and depth/pretraining controls. Section 4.4 and Appendix D examine retrieval efficiency and whether gains merely reflect additional model depth or depend on pretraining.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed/run counts, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests for forecasting results. v2's checklist explicitly acknowledges the absence of significance reporting but adds no statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Existing forecasting scores and plotted results are retained. New Table 2 reports Traffic retrieval overheads of 0.079 s for cosine versus 87.957 s for LSH, both with 0.025 MSE improvement. Table 7 adds depth/scratch results; PIR generally performs better, but Electricity at horizon 720 favors the deeper model in MSE, 0.217 versus PIR's 0.219.

T1.justification: Section 4.4 adds a brief complexity analysis: O(N M L_in) for cosine retrieval and O(N^2) for channel-wise attention. Existing mathematical definitions and Equations (1)-(7) remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about instance-level forecasting failures and model-agnostic identification and revision using local/global context. The additional analyses support those claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v2 explains that failure causes cannot be disentangled without suitable ground truth and metrics. It also attributes cosine efficiency to GPU parallelism and suggests unstable early backbone forecasts as a possible explanation for scratch-training degradation. Appendix F's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds reported code and running-script access links, identifies FAISS for the LSH implementation, and explicitly discusses the pretrained-backbone requirement. Existing hardware, optimizer, retrieval-count search and auxiliary-loss-weight disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds two papers on LLM reasoning for forecasting. It removes the RAF citation by Tire et al. and adds discussions of RATSF and RAFT by Han et al. The central positioning of PIR as a post-forecasting correction framework remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes local explanatory edits, adds a complexity subsection, acknowledgments and a NeurIPS checklist, and updates author/conference notices. The existing scientific narrative and organization of Appendices A-F remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the inference-time table and the depth/pretraining ablation table. Existing appendix tables are renumbered, and Figures 6 and 7 are relocated together onto one page. The original figures and table structures are otherwise preserved.

improvement.justification: The runtime analysis and depth/pretraining controls make computational cost and sources of improvement easier to assess, while code-access information improves reproducibility documentation. These are useful incremental gains. However, Appendix D overstates consistent superiority despite Table 7's exceptions, and statistical uncertainty remains unreported.
